ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.AEFiniteKernelS.issue: Definition body is shown but the English only paraphrases the docstring. It should state the body: for μ-a.e. t there is a finite set A ⊆ S with κ(t)(Aᶜ) = 0. 'κ(t) has finite support' is only the docstring's gloss.

Definition body is shown but the English gives no description of the kernel, only the docstring remark that hκ is unused. It omits the body: if S is nonempty, the piecewise kernel equal to κ on {t | ∃ finite A, κ t Aᶜ = 0} and to the constant Dirac kernel at a chosen point elsewhere; otherwise the zero kernel.

ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.FiniteKernelSup.issue: Definition body is shown but the English only repeats the docstring ('analogue of FiniteSupport for probability kernels'). It never states the body: for every t there is a finite A ⊆ S with κ(t)(Aᶜ) = 0. The docstring's 'probability kernels' is also misleading, since the definition applies to any kernel.

ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.aefiniteKernelS.issue: The symbols κ.condKernel, κ.fst and μ⊗κ.fst are used without being introduced; the reader is not told that κ.fst is the first marginal, that condKernel is the conditional kernel T×S → U, or that ⊗ is the measure-kernel composition-product rather than a product measure. The project notion AEFiniteKernelSupport is also used without saying what it means (for a.e. point there is a finite set of full measure).
